pairs.left_when: Ready eligible requests have no binding due interval: choose their service discipline.
pairs.right_when: A known completion deadline or future release excludes an otherwise attractive queue order; temporal feasibility comes first.

pairs.left_when: Service units resume without occupied switch intervals and the target is wait or entitlement.
pairs.right_when: Family changes consume two processor units, as in BOC01; compare setup occupancy before accepting a discipline.

pairs.left_when: The eligible ready set is already valid; choose between its competing requests.
pairs.right_when: Known A→B excludes B from the ready set even when B has higher priority.

pairs.left_when: Every selected task already has its required input.
pairs.right_when: A converter, authorization or producer is missing from the task description; extract that dependency before ranking.

pairs.left_when: The work is an ongoing queue with a supplied goal.
pairs.right_when: The open decision is how much effort a one-off indifferent queue choice warrants.

pairs.left_when: The actual target has declared retained progress or reset behavior.
pairs.right_when: Resumable CPU service is only a proposed analogy for a different activity with unknown restart behavior.

pairs.left_when: Several still-required products compete for service.
pairs.right_when: The acceptance criterion is already met and the issue is whether another queued item is needed.

pairs.left_when: Priorities, weights and resources are available inputs.
pairs.right_when: The entitlement weight or resource access decision remains unmade; order the needed resolutions.

pairs.left_when: Changing an order can violate a due time; retain deadline admissibility even if another order has fewer setups.
pairs.right_when: Every relevant due time is slack and occupied setup or bottleneck capacity controls the comparison. With both present, feasibility precedes resource optimization.

pairs.left_when: A valid dependency order still needs actual start/finish positions relative to a deadline.
pairs.right_when: Only predecessor-before-successor validity is required and there is no duration or deadline objective.

pairs.left_when: Durations, due times and required predecessors are known.
pairs.right_when: A supposed starting task needs an unlisted input; the temporal plan cannot be formed until that input relation exists.

pairs.left_when: A schedule must place actual work before a known closing time.
pairs.right_when: The question is whether to spend two minutes or a longer effort budget selecting a schedule; timing arithmetic alone does not choose that budget.

pairs.left_when: The due time and nonpreemption relation are actual target inputs.
pairs.right_when: A source due-time example is being carried into a domain where the meaning of completion differs.

pairs.left_when: All listed deliverables remain mandatory and must fit before the closing time.
pairs.right_when: The candidate way to fit is dropping or stopping a deliverable; sufficiency must establish whether that changes the required result.

pairs.left_when: The closing time is fixed and available.
pairs.right_when: Access duration and the decision to change location await answers that determine which deadlines exist.

pairs.left_when: Tasks without logical edges still share one mutable file or one occupied processor.
pairs.right_when: Separate resources are genuinely available and only hard task predecessors prevent parallel work.

pairs.left_when: Resource occupancy and all task inputs are known; calculate bottlenecks and setups.
pairs.right_when: The apparent resource problem is actually an unlisted producer/consumer input relation.

pairs.left_when: The object is the operating stream: service, switching and waits.
pairs.right_when: The object is the effort invested in choosing an optimization; another pass has no decision-changing result.

pairs.left_when: The capacity, setup and reset semantics are specified for this target.
pairs.right_when: An engineering bottleneck is being treated as a person’s attention limit without a tested correspondence.

pairs.left_when: Required tasks are fixed, so waste is occupied overhead around those tasks.
pairs.right_when: A proposed efficiency gain deletes a substantive required output; evaluate sufficiency before calling it waste.

pairs.left_when: The processor and current family are known, enabling the BOC setup calculation.
pairs.right_when: Availability of a second resource is unconfirmed and would remove the present bottleneck.

pairs.left_when: The supplied graph already states each input dependency; generate a valid sequence.
pairs.right_when: The input contains only task names or ambiguous arrows; establish which output feeds which task first.

pairs.left_when: The required graph has a meaningful readiness problem.
pairs.right_when: Two independent interchangeable tasks have no ordering consequence; the decision warrants only a minimal choice.

pairs.left_when: The dependency relation is native to the workflow and already established.
pairs.right_when: A chess or CPU ordering relation is being proposed for a different target; establish its mapping before sorting.

pairs.left_when: Every graph node is still part of the necessary output.
pairs.right_when: A whole subgraph is optional and the open question is whether the achieved result is sufficient without it.

pairs.left_when: Nodes are executable tasks with settled specifications.
pairs.right_when: Nodes are unresolved decisions; one answer changes or eliminates the options of another.

pairs.left_when: A missing prerequisite blocks an actual output, so its input/output relation must be found.
pairs.right_when: Nothing is blocked and the choice is an indifferent reversible tie; an exhaustive dependency inventory changes no action.

pairs.left_when: The work is within one workflow: identify which artifact or state a task consumes.
pairs.right_when: The work compares source and target relationships, including disanalogies between domains.

pairs.left_when: The question is what an unfinished task requires to start.
pairs.right_when: The question is whether the already-built result meets its purpose across breadth, depth, quality, validation and robustness.

pairs.left_when: Task prerequisites are missing from the representation.
pairs.right_when: The unresolved decisions and their possible cascades are already the objects to be sequenced.

pairs.left_when: The transfer question is already definite and the pending choice concerns the effort budget.
pairs.right_when: The mapping itself is unsupported; a fast decision cannot supply missing correspondences or a target test.

pairs.left_when: No substantial analysis exists yet; choose an effort level from stakes and reversibility.
pairs.right_when: An existing analysis can be compared with its declared purpose and specific remaining gaps.

pairs.left_when: One definite decision needs a proportionate effort level.
pairs.right_when: Several unresolved decisions constrain each other’s possible answers and need an operational resolution order.

pairs.left_when: A source principle has not yet been validated in the new target; derive and test a transfer hypothesis.
pairs.right_when: The target application exists and the issue is whether its evidence covers the intended scope.

pairs.left_when: The correspondence between domains is the uncertain substantive relation.
pairs.right_when: The missing item is a supplied user rating, access decision or assigned choice; mapping cannot invent that external input.

pairs.left_when: A finished candidate is being compared with a fixed acceptance standard.
pairs.right_when: Specific missing decisions already prevent completion and must be assigned in an order that respects cascades.
